metadata.note: The Milwaukee Road's Twin Cities Hiawatha, the historical predecessor of both Amtrak's Hiawatha Service (Chicago-Milwaukee) and its Borealis (Chicago-Twin Cities), which together cover the same corridor. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; any place where the historical routing differed is described in the segment notes and reflected in the geometry. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones (train introductions, renamings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Twin Cities Hiawatha, Hiawatha - Milwaukee Road trains), american-rails.com, trains.com
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Milwaukee & St. Paul Railway acquired the St. Paul & Chicago Railway in 1872 (which had just completed the west-bank-of-the-Mississippi route from St. Paul to La Crescent, opposite La Crosse), then completed its own Milwaukee-Chicago line in 1873, creating a full through Chicago-Twin Cities route under one company for the first time (renamed Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul Railway in 1874). Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Minneapolis-St. Paul boomed into one of the country's great rail hubs in this era - nine railroads (Great Northern, Northern Pacific, Rock Island, Minneapolis & St. Louis, Milwaukee, Omaha, Burlington, Soo Line, Chicago Great West) served the Twin Cities, with a record 174 intercity trains a day originating, terminating, or passing through by 1916. Renamed Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific Railroad in 1928 after the Pacific extension. Frequency on this specific Chicago-Twin Cities corridor estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The Hiawatha entered service May 29 1935 between Chicago, Milwaukee and the Twin Cities - one of the first streamliners in the US, built entirely in the Milwaukee Road's own shops and hauled by streamlined 4-4-2 Atlantics, regularly running over 100 mph. Launched to counter streamliners then under development by the CB&Q and the Chicago & North Western. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: So successful the railroad ran two daily versions, the Morning Hiawatha and Afternoon Hiawatha, later hauled by 4-6-4 Hudsons. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
